REQUEST
The applicant is requesting approval to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site
consumption from an existing convenience market at 400 West Manchester Boulevard.

BACKGROUND
Chapter 12, Articles 7 and 25 of the IMC require Special Use Permit approval for the
sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption within the C-2 (General Commercial)
zone.

Site Characteristics and Existing Use
The subject site is located at the southwest corner of Manchester Boulevard and
Inglewood Avenue. The site is developed with an existing shopping center that was built
in 1985. The shopping center contains six (6) tenant spaces with associated on-site
parking. There is one driveway on the north side of the lot, providing access from
Manchester Boulevard, and an additional vehicular driveway is provided from Inglewood
Avenue to the east. Existing uses at the site include two (2) restaurants, a nail salon, a
barber shop, and the applicant’s existing convenience market. The existing convenience
market has been active since June 2019, and was previously licensed as a liquor store
from 1985 to 2016.

DISCUSSION
Within the approximately 1,208 square-foot convenience market, the majority of floor
area will continue to be used for display of general merchandise and limited grocery
sales such as milk, juice, bread, cereal, chips, canned foods, household items, toiletries,
magazines, and newspapers displayed over several shelving units and wall displays.

The beer and wine will be available to customers in a section of an existing wall of
cooler doors located in the rear of the store. The beer and wine will be within three (3) of
the existing eight (8) cooler doors and the coolers containing the alcohol will be locked
and opened for customers by an employee with a key on an as-needed basis. Non-
alcoholic beverages will continue to be available in the adjacent, but separate, five-door
beverage cooler. The applicant is also a proposing a separate locked enclosure to
display non-refrigerated wine. The proposed beer and wine sales area would occupy
approximately 40 square-feet which constitutes approximately three percent of the total
market floor area. The Planning Commission can limit the sales area as part of this
application to ensure that the sales area remains under a specified amount of the floor
area.

The hours of operation for the convenience market and proposed beer and wine sales
are 7:00 a.m. to 1:00 a.m., seven days a week. The convenience market will have a
total of three (3) employees on site at all times.

Surrounding ABC Licenses
According to the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC), two (2)
off-sale licenses are permitted within the subject site’s Census Tract (Census Tract
6014.01) without the Census Tract being considered over concentrated. ABC records
indicate that there are currently seven (7) active licensees; five (5) Type 20 (Off-sale
Beer and Wine) and two (2) Type 21 (Off-sale General) license:

Area Compatibility & Crime
The site is developed in accordance with existing zoning and development standards for
building height and setbacks for commercially-zoned properties. Surrounding land uses
along Manchester Boulevard are developed primarily with commercial uses. South of
the site, along Inglewood Avenue, are legal non-conforming residential uses and a child
care facility.

In the subject Crime Reporting District (CRD), No. I-15, the crime rate decreased from
82 incidents in 2016 to 60 incidents in 2018. The subject site has maintained a low
crime rate with zero incidents in 2016, 2017, and 2018. Details on the statistics for the
CRD and subject site can be found below in Table 2. Since the subject site is located on
the border of two additional CRDs, details on the surrounding CRDs (08 and 17) are
provided in Attachment 4.

Public Convenience or Necessity Determination
Based on the existing ABC licenses in the area, the Planning Commission as part of its
consideration of this SUP request will need to make a finding whether or not the
proposed ABC license provides a public convenience or necessity to the community.
The applicant has submitted their justification in regards to Public Convenience or
Necessity (Attachment 5). In summary, the applicant’s justification states that the
proposed alcohol sales will provide Public Convenience or Necessity due to the existing
mini-mart’s business model, focused on convenience, as opposed to “big box” retailers
or businesses specializing fully in alcohol sales. The availability of the beer and wine will
offer a broader range of goods to the surrounding community.

Site Design
The convenience market’s footprint and circulation will not be altered. Pedestrian
access into the market will remain unchanged with the entrance oriented towards the
parking area.
 Special Use Permit No. 2019-014 (SP-2019-014)  December 4, 2019
400 West Manchester Boulevard
Page 5 of 6

Parking and Circulation
No change is proposed to the existing access and no change to the existing traffic level
of service is anticipated. The existing center has 24 parking spaces, which complies
with IMC parking requirements, therefore, the site will continue to have adequate
parking for the convenience market.

Security
There are currently eight (8) security cameras for the interior of the store and three (3)
security cameras for the exterior of the store. The cameras are monitored in real time
and will be shared with the Inglewood Police Department upon request.

Landscaping
Existing landscaping is provided within the existing landscaped planters along the street
frontage adjacent to the public right of way on Manchester Boulevard and Inglewood
Avenue. No change is proposed to the existing landscaping.

Site Plan Review
If approved, a Site Plan Review will be required and the following requirements will be
applied:
   Provide a trash enclosure for the subject site
   Install utility screening with a solid decorative wall, fence, or landscaping

Public Comments
As of the preparation of this report, no public comments in favor or against this project
have been received.

General Plan Consistency
The proposed project is consistent with the Commercial land use designation of the
General Plan in that it ensures the availability of commercial goods and services for the
needs of the residents and businesses in the community.

Environmental Determination
A Notice of Exemption (EA-CE-2019-127) has been prepared by staff stating that the
proposed project is exempt from further environmental review, a copy of which has
been available for review in the Planning Division office located on the fourth floor of
City  Hall.  An  electronic  copy  is  available  by  email  request  to
mfewell@cityofinglewood.org.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 4, 2019

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, December 4, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Chairman Larry Springs
Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Terry Coleman

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox mentioned the Planning Division / Planning Commission
Annual Holiday Luncheon, the location and the Tour of the New Sofi
Stadium, which is scheduled for Monday, December 9, 2019 and the
information will be emailed to each Planning Commissioner and
Chair, along with staff.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-010 (SP-2019-010) AT 1500-1502
NORTH LA BREA AVENUE. A continued public hearing to consider an
application by Matt Budney, representing 7-Eleven, for Special Use
Permit No. 2019-010 (SP-2019-010) to allow 1) an automobile service
station and 2) the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption
from a proposed convenience market on an approximately 23,100
square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 1500-1502
North La Brea Avenue. The applicant requests that this item be
continued to the February 5, 2020, Planning Commission Meeting.

MOTION:

The motion was made by Commissioner Rice for approval of a
continuation of Item 5A Special Use Permit No. 2019-010 (SP-2019-
010) to the February 5, 2020 Planning Commission meeting and was
seconded by Commissioner Holly.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioner Holly, Rice, Trejo and Chairman Springs
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 4, 2019

Chairman Springs made an announcement to the audience/community
members in attendance for the Item 5A, to inform them that it has
been motioned and approved to be continued until the February 5,
2020 Planning Commission and if there was a desire to speak on
this item, at the end of this Planning Commission meeting, they
may speak at that time.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-014 (SP-2019-014), 400 WEST
MANCHESTER BLVD. A public hearing to consider an application by
Maninder Kaur, representing Jas & Sam, Inc., for Special Use Permit
No. 2019-014 (SP-2019-014) to allow the sale of beer and wine for
off-site consumption from an existing convenience market on an
approximately 17,500 square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned
property at 400 West Manchester Boulevard.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 Regarding the 7/11 across the street, which is within 500 feet,
  what are the hours of the 7/11 operation and is there any time
  constraints on alcohol sales?
  - Commissioner Holly stated a 7/11 is open 24 hours a day.
  - Ms. Fewell stated that 7/11 might have the same ABC
  restrictions for alcohol sales of 6:00am until 2:00am.
 This store was previously opened from 1985 until 2016, does
  staff know the reason it was closed for so long?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that she did not know why.
 If this application is approved will the applicant be required
  to sell the alcohol in case quantities or are they able to sell
  small single containers?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant cannot sell anything
  less than 24 ounces nor anything larger than 32 ounces, per
  the resolution condition no. 13.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
the planning commission.

Ms. Maninder Kaur, representing Jas & Sam, Inc., addressed the
planning commission with her presentation regarding the site. She
stated that the sole purpose for purchasing the store was because
it was in the past a liquor store, and they were first told that
they could purchase the previous owner’s license for the sale of
beer and wine, but once purchased, they were told it was a mistake
and that they would have to apply for a new permit after all. They
noticed that the majority of the customers who came into the store
are looking for the old liquor store that used to be there. Once
the customers found out that the liquor store is no more, just a
convenience grocery store, they leave the items that they were
going to purchase, anywhere in the store or at the counter, and
leave the store. It is very difficult to make a living with a store
where the customers will not purchase other products from you
because you do not have beer or wine, in order to make it a one
stop shop.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for questions to the applicants
by the planning commission.

Commissioner Holly asked:
 When looking at the outside of the building its exterior gives
  a very negative connotation and it would better the community
  by sprucing up and changing the sign that is on the roof of the
  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 4, 2019
  building. The sign is very old and needs clearing up, cleaning,
  upgrading and beautifying, what, if your application is
  approved, would you do to beautify the outside of the building,
  along with the sign on and around the top of the property and
  for the neighborhood?
  - Ms. Kaur stated that their intention is to change the name
  and look of the sign on the roof, but were waiting to see if
  they would be approved for the beer and wine license first,
  because they want to include it with the title of the new
  sign.

Commissioner Rice stated his question to staff:
 What is the percentage of signage allowed for this tenant at
  that location on their building?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that it is approximately 3 square-feet per
  foot of lot frontage, so in the case of this shopping center,
  you would take all the lot frontage (whatever that number is)
  and multiply it by three and that is the total square footage
  that the entire site is permitted, then it is broken up by
  each individual tenant, the landlord puts together a Master
  Sign program, but divides up that percentage. As this process
  would go through site plan review we would insure that any
  signage that is not permitted is legalized. We have not looked
  at that closely to see if the signs have been permitted or
  not, but that would be part of the review.

Commissioner Trejo asked:
 She also noticed the broken-down sign on the east side of the
  building that needs to be replaced.
  - Ms. Kaur stated that sign will be replaced and we were waiting
  to see what the outcome would be from the meeting tonight and
  then our plan was to make a nice new sign.
 Following up on the question of our chairman, there has to be a
  finding of convenience or necessity to the surrounding
  neighborhood as to why there needs to be another beer and wine
  license approved for the area when if approved would cause an
  over-concentration of licenses. As per Alcohol & Beverage
  Control (ABC) says that when a census tract is over-concentrated
  and since there are already two licenses that are permitted for
  this census tract, there needs to be shown a finding of public
  convenience or necessity and as of yet this has not been
  demonstrated or stated. The 7/11 has the same benefits and
  conveniences that the applicant has and as such shows no
  necessity for a third beer and wine license.
  - Ms. Kaur stated that the customers come to their store for
  the groceries, which that would be maybe 80-85% of their
  shopping and the balance would be for the beer and wine. At
  our store the local community does not have to drive to go to
  a grocery store for their products, we are within walking
  distance for the community, and we have a great variety of
  products, that is how we are different and serve a great
  convenience for our neighborhood.
 She stated that the other stores in the area have the same
  conveniences already and they already have their license and
  that is what is being stated here that the census tract is
  already full. Also the applicant has submitted a letter and it
  is addressing what the applicant feels is public convenience
  and necessity, it states “the area needs much more well-
  established restaurants”, so how does that fit into what your
  store is offering?
  - Mr. Franco Jas approached to answer the question from the
  Commissioner.

  3

Commissioner Trejo states;
 She would ask her question once again and asked staff if they
  provided a copy of the letter that is in question, to Mr. Jas
  and Staff stated yes.
 She stated that at the bottom of the letter that was submitted
  to staff for the planning commission to convince the planning
  commission that their store offers convenience and necessity to
  the neighborhood, there is a statement and the statement says
  “the area needs much more well-established restaurants”, and
  she wants to know what does this statement have to do with what
  was being asked by staff about their grocery store?
  - Mr. Jas thought that it was a question regarding restaurants
  in the area, and was not directing it towards what their
  grocery store is providing to the local neighborhood and no
  they are not promoting a restaurant in their store. It was a
  misunderstanding.
 She stated she was just trying to get clarification. Thank you.

Chairman Springs stated his questions to the applicant;
 What is being sold at your market that is not being sold at
  others in the area? Are you selling produce, meats?
  - Ms. Kaur stated all items of a convenience mini mart, with
  dairy, yogurt, cheeses, packaged sandwiches, sodas, drinks,
  home cleaning supplies.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments to speak
for or against this project, with the announcement of two minutes.

FOR / AGAINST

  Larry Richardson – Inglewood Resident, For

Chairman Springs closed public comments, called for questions and
final remarks from the planning commission.

Commissioner Rice stated – He wanted to speak to the applicant
once again.
 He stated to Ms. Kaur that he wanted to make sure that she
  clearly understands what the Planning Commission is tasked to
  do on this evening. How they have to see that their mini-mart
  will be of a necessity and convenience to the community, where
  what you are offering is completely different from what everyone
  else around your store is selling, because of the over-
  saturation of beer and wine licenses that the applicant is
  asking for. Does your store offer anything else that would be
  distinguished only at your mini-mart that no one else is
  offering, that can convince this planning commission to move in
  favor of your behalf?
  - Ms. Kaur continued to state that what they have in their store
  although it may be similar to 7/11, it makes it convenient to
  the customer to only have to stop at one store on the way
  home by being able to pick up all grocery needs along with
  either beer or wine and then go straight home.
 He stated that would it be fair to say that if the applicant is
  granted the beer and wine license, it would help the applicant
  to be competitive with the surrounding like businesses?
  - Ms. Kaur said that the customers are continuing to ask when
  will their store obtain their license for beer and wine,
  because they have to travel to two stores to fulfill their
  shopping needs, once they have finished with her mini-mart,
  then they have to go across the street to the crowded 7/11
  which it is always crowded, to obtain their beer and wine and
  they don’t like doing this. It is for their convenience that
  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 4, 2019
  we obtain the beer and wine license in order for their
  customers will only have to do a one-stop shop.

Chairman Springs stated he also had another question for the
applicant and asks her to wait -
 If the beer and wine license is not approved and if the planning
  commission denies the application, will it hurt or hinder your
  business from making profits?
  - Ms. Kaur stated yes it will hinder our business. Many of our
  customers ask when they come in while they are getting their
  groceries, if we have beer and wine license yet and when we
  tell them no, not yet, they immediately put down their
  groceries, not even putting them back where they found them
  and leave the store stating they are disappointed that they
  now have to go farther to another store just to do all their
  shopping in one location.

Chairman Springs called for any questions and asked for a motion
from the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Trejo stated that she will make the motion, but she
had a statement for the applicant first.
- The Planning Commission understands that your business is trying
  to be successful and competitive and as the Planning Commission
  we all want businesses in this City to succeed, however, we also
  have to follow direction and rules from in this case, Alcoholic
  & Beverage Control (ABC), as to how and when liquor licenses
  can be issued and again in this case we do not see anything that
  is different than any of the other and already over-concentrated
  census tract provides.

MOTION:

The motion was made by Commissioner Trejo to deny the request for
Special Use Permit No. 2019-014 (SP-2019-014) and not affirm
Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2019-127 and not adopt the attached
resolution approving SP-2019-014, and not allow the sale of beer
and wine for off-site consumption in an existing convenience market
located at 400 West Manchester Boulevard, in Census Tract 6014.1.
The granting of such request would be detrimental to the immediate
neighborhood, because it would add to the already over-
concentrated number of licenses in the Census Tract. ABC permits
two (2) off-sale licenses before a Census Tract is considered over-
concentrated, here there are already seven (7) active licenses in
the Census Tract, thus there is no question that the Census Tract
is over-concentrated with the permitted ABC licenses. The required
finding that must be made when there is over-concentration, is
that the granting of a request to add an additional license will
provide a public convenience or necessity and that was not
demonstrated. That findings cannot be made with regards to this
applicant, particularly since two (2) of those seven (7) licenses
are within a 500-foot buffer of the subject site and they are
already substantially providing the same type of service as that
proposed by the applicant. Additionally, the applicant has not
sufficiently demonstrated that adding one more off-sale license to
an already over-concentrated Census Tract will provide a public
convenience or necessity and was seconded by Commissioner Rice,
that Resolution No. 1853;

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioner Rice, Trejo and Chairman Springs

No:  Commissioner Holly

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal period.

(6) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

1. Veronica Ulloa – Inglewood Resident – Question about the number
  of liquor licenses in a census tract.

2. Ms. Maninder Kaur – Applicant of Item 5B asking if the Planning
  Commission will reconsider their decision of Denial.

Chairman Springs stated that Commissioner Trejo will answer both
Ms. Ulloa and Ms. Kaur’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo answered the question of Ms. Ulloa and Ms. Kaur
by reading her findings regarding census tract determinations.

  ABC permits two (2) off-sale licenses before a Census Tract is
  considered over-concentrated, here there are already seven (7)
  active licenses in the Census Tract, thus there is no question
  that the Census Tract is over-concentrated with the permitted
  ABC licenses.

So when there is an over-concentration a specific finding has to
be made by the planning commission in order to allow an additional
license within that particular census tract. Again it may be
different somewhere else, but in this one that we are talking about
that is the rule.

Ms. Wilcox stated to Chairman, that if there are any further
questions or concerns, staff will be available after the meeting
to answer the questions.

Chairman Springs stated that Staff will assist with any further
questions regarding the census tract and the Planning Commissions’
Denial decision and any information they seek regarding appealing
the decision.

Chairman Springs asked if there was anyone else who wanted to
speak, to come to the microphone.

3. Carol Bray – Inglewood Resident – Against 7/11-Item 5A.

4. Jackie Swarte – Inglewood Resident – Against 7/11-Item 5A.

5. Robert Leveen – Inglewood Resident – Against 7/11-Item 5A.

(7) COMMISSION ANNITIATIVES:

Commissioner Holly said Thank Everyone for coming this evening and
have Safe Holiday’s to all.

Commissioner Trejo stated although sometimes tough and hard
decisions have to be made, everything will work out and hopes that
all will be Safe and have a very Happy Holiday.

(8) ADJOURNMENT:

Chairman Springs wanted to thank everyone for coming out and hope
that all realize the true meaning of Christmas and to Ms. Kaur,
that with Staff’s assistance all answers will be given and now
this meeting stands adjourned at 7:45pm.
